therapeuticClass: Addiction Medicine — Opioid Partial Agonist — Schedule III Controlled Substance — Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT)
indication: Opioid use disorder (OUD) — induction, stabilization, and maintenance treatment as part of a comprehensive Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) program; opioid dependence
quantityLimit: 60 films per 30-day supply (2 films/day maximum for maintenance dosing)
quantityLimitReason: Standard maintenance dose range is 4–24 mg/day. 60-film limit per 30 days supports doses up to 16 mg twice daily. Higher doses require QL exception with documentation of patient response and prescriber clinical justification.
formularyNotes: HealthBridge covers buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone film and generic equivalent) for OUD treatment as part of a Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) plan. Per Illinois Mental Health Parity law and federal ACA requirements, SUD treatment benefits must be comparable to medical/surgical benefits. PA required to ensure appropriate MAT program enrollment (prescriber must have DEA X-waiver or DATA 2000 waiver). Brand Suboxone is Tier 3; generic sublingual film is Tier 2. Tablet formulation (Zubsolv) is Tier 2.
priorAuthCriteria: Diagnosis of Opioid Use Disorder (ICD-10: F11.20, F11.21, F11.22) documented
Prescriber holds valid DEA Schedule III license and applicable buprenorphine prescribing waiver
Enrollment in or referral to comprehensive MAT program including counseling component
Initial authorization: 90 days; renewal: 12 months with documented compliance and treatment response
clinicalAlerts: Schedule III — prescribers must hold DEA Schedule III license and applicable DATA 2000 waiver for OUD treatment
Risk of diversion — monitor for signs of misuse; urine drug screening recommended
Buprenorphine causes partial mu-opioid agonism — precipitated withdrawal if administered too soon after full agonist opioid
Mail-order available for stable maintenance patients
